title: PBR Fundamentals: The Metallic/Roughness Workflow
body: Physically Based Rendering represents surfaces with Base Color, Metallic, and Roughness maps under the metal/rough workflow used by Unreal, Unity, and Substance. Metallic is nearly binary in practice (0 or 1 for most real materials, with only a few transitional pixels at edges/rust). Roughness controls the microfacet distribution of the surface and drives how sharp or diffuse specular reflections appear.

title: Texture Channel Reference
body: Base Color: albedo with no baked lighting. Roughness: grayscale microsurface detail. Metallic: grayscale, near-binary. Normal: tangent-space RGB encoding surface direction (OpenGL vs DirectX Y-channel differs). Height: grayscale displacement/parallax source. Ambient Occlusion: grayscale contact shadowing, never baked into Base Color. Emission: HDR-capable self-illumination. ORM: Occlusion/Roughness/Metallic packed into R/G/B of a single texture, common in glTF and Unreal mobile pipelines.

title: Stone & Rock Material Notes
body: Stone surfaces are typically fully dielectric (Metallic = 0). Roughness varies widely: polished marble sits low (0.1-0.3), weathered granite or sandstone sits high (0.6-0.9). Watch for baked AO in Base Color from poorly-lit source photography, which flattens the material under new lighting.

title: Metal Material Notes
body: Raw, unpainted metal is Metallic = 1 with Base Color driven by the metal's reflectance color rather than a diffuse albedo. Painted or rusted metal is a mixed/layered material: painted regions read as dielectric (Metallic near 0) while exposed metal or scratches spike back to 1. Roughness is the primary read for wear.

title: Wood Material Notes
body: Wood is dielectric (Metallic = 0). Varnished/lacquered wood has low, uniform roughness with a subtle clearcoat-like specular response; raw or weathered wood has higher, more variable roughness following the grain direction, which should also drive normal map detail.

title: Fabric Material Notes
body: Fabrics are dielectric with consistently high roughness. Fine weave detail is usually better represented in the normal and height maps than by fighting for it in Base Color resolution. Consider a dedicated sheen/fuzz shader model for velvet or felt where standard PBR under-represents grazing-angle brightness.

title: Substance Painter Production Notes
body: Bake mesh maps (AO, curvature, position, normal) before hand-painting masks so generators and smart materials respond correctly to edges and cavities. Export presets should match the target engine's channel packing exactly (e.g., Unreal's ORM packing) to avoid a manual repack step.

title: Substance Designer Production Notes
body: Favor procedural, resolution-independent graphs for tileable base materials so the same graph can be re-exported at multiple target resolutions without redoing work. Keep height/displacement ranges physically plausible relative to the mesh scale to avoid exaggerated parallax artifacts.

title: Unreal Engine Texture Optimization Notes
body: Pack Occlusion/Roughness/Metallic into a single ORM texture to cut one full texture sample per material on mobile and console. Use BC7 for high-fidelity Base Color/Normal on PC/console, and ASTC on mobile. Keep Normal maps uncompressed or BC5 to avoid banding.

title: Unity Texture Optimization Notes
body: Unity's Standard/URP metallic workflow expects Metallic in the Red channel and Smoothness (inverse roughness) in the Alpha channel of the same texture, which is a common source of inverted-roughness bugs when importing assets authored for the roughness convention elsewhere.
